content.value_statement: Independent failures can slow review when each issue waits for a single investigation. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code split scoped work across parallel agents.
actual_capabilities: Identifies when failures are independent enough for parallel investigation.
Defines separate agent scopes by file, directory, or subsystem.
Provides a Task-based dispatch pattern for concurrent agent work.
Supplies a reusable agent prompt structure with task, scope, goal, constraints, and output.
Guides result integration with root cause, changes, tests, and conflict checks.
limitations: It is not suited for failures that share one root cause.
It does not provide automated scheduling or merge tooling.
It depends on available agent tools and workspace permissions.
It requires clear scopes to avoid overlapping edits.

use_cases.title: Split Independent Test Failures
use_cases.description: Assign unrelated test failures to separate agents so each investigation stays focused and bounded.
use_cases.target_user: Software engineers maintaining large test suites

use_cases.title: Coordinate Modular Bug Fixes
use_cases.description: Give each agent one module, goal, and constraint set before combining the resulting fixes.

use_cases.title: Review Multi-Area Regressions
use_cases.description: Investigate regressions across separate subsystems without forcing one agent to hold every context detail.

prompt_templates.title: Check If Work Can Be Split
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review these failures. Tell me whether they are independent enough for parallel agents, and list the proposed scopes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Agent Assignments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create one agent assignment per independent problem. Include task, scope, goal, constraints, and expected output for each agent.

prompt_templates.title: Dispatch And Integrate Results
prompt_templates.scenario: Run parallel investigations and merge findings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to dispatch agents for these independent failures. After they finish, summarize root causes, changes, tests, and any edit conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Large Parallel Debugging Pass
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced use for a broad failing suite.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to partition this failing suite into safe parallel workstreams. Define boundaries, shared constraints, verification steps, and integration order.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated failures affect authentication, API routing, and database connection tests.
output_examples.output: The skill produces three scoped agent assignments, one per subsystem, with boundaries, goals, constraints, and expected result summaries.

output_examples.input: Six failures appear across three files after a refactor.
output_examples.output: The skill groups failures by file area, dispatches parallel investigations, then reports root causes, fixes, test outcomes, and conflicts.

output_examples.input: A user wants faster debugging but is unsure which tasks can run together.
output_examples.output: The skill separates independent tasks from coupled tasks and recommends parallel agents only for the independent set.

best_practices: Use this skill only after grouping failures by file, subsystem, or root cause hypothesis.
Give each agent strict edit boundaries and the same verification expectations.
Integrate results with a final conflict check and a unified test run.
anti_patterns: Do not dispatch agents for failures that likely share one root cause.
Do not let multiple agents edit the same files without coordination.
Do not omit constraints, expected output, or verification requirements.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when at least three failures are independent and can be investigated without shared state.

faq.question: Does it run agents automatically?
faq.answer: It provides an orchestration pattern and prompt structure. Actual execution depends on the available agent tools.

faq.question: Can it handle one complex failure?
faq.answer: No. A single complex failure usually needs one focused investigation with full context.

faq.question: How does it reduce conflicts?
faq.answer: It asks for narrow file or subsystem scopes and explicit constraints for each agent.

faq.question: Is it useful outside software debugging?
faq.answer: Yes, if the work can be split into independent domains with clear outputs and no shared state.

faq.question: What should I review after agents finish?
faq.answer: Review root causes, changed areas, test results, conflicts, and whether the combined fix still passes verification.
